US Calls In Scots Drugs Expert
A LEADING researcher into drug misuse has been invited to Washington by George W Bush's drugs czar to discuss the health dangers of cannabis.

Professor Neil McKeganey, director of the centre for drugs misuse research at Glasgow University, will meet a team of mental health experts, scientists and high-ranking US government officials to discuss an emerging body of research that identifies links between cannabis use and mental-health disorders among teenagers.

Mr McKeganey points to a " clear distance " between the US government's approach to cannabis misuse and those of Westminster and the Scottish Executive, and warns that the possible dangers of the drug, including depression and schizophrenia, could be overlooked in Britain should research and policy continue to focus on the " more dramatic impacts " of heroin and cocaine use.

Maybe We've Got It Wrong

Scotland has one of the highest levels of cannabis use in Europe, with around 50% of 15-year-olds having smoked the drug and around 25% smoking the drug on a regular basis. In the light of those figures, it is arguable whether we should be doing anything which might further increase the level of cannabis use when what we should be doing is increasing our efforts at drug prevention.

WARNING OVER 'FORGOTTEN' DRUG
By Jim McBeth

ONE of Scotland's leading drugs experts has called for cannabis use among young people to be put at the very forefront of the debate on substance abuse

Professor Neil McKeganey, director of the centre for drug misuse research in Glasgow, has spoken out on the dangers of assuming cannabis is one of the least harmful drugs and its subsequent prevalence among young people.

Prof McKeganey said: " Our level of cannabis use is among the highest in Europe. The young do not see it as a notable drug and that is hugely worrying. We must put the cannabis debate back to the forefront. "

Official figures suggest cannabis use has risen yearly for a decade and caused a 60 per cent increase in health problems.

Excerpted from the January 2, 2003 Independent (London)

Scotland's relationship with drink is 'spinning out of control' By Paul Kelbie Scotland Correspondent

A culture of binge drinking means that alcohol is killing four times as many Scots as it did a generation ago, costing the country more than £1bn a year.

Latest statistics from the Department of Health reveal that one in four women aged between 18 and 24 now drinks to excess, compared with one in eight a decade ago, prompting Scotland's deputy chief medical officer, Dr Andrew Fraser, to warn the problem is on the verge of spinning out of control. " Other countries don't drink the way we drink, " said Dr Fraser. " We have to relearn our relationship with alcohol. "

One area of Glasgow has been named as having the world's highest incidence of a rare type of alcohol-related brain damage. Korsakov's syndrome is an irreversible condition that causes patients to lose their short-term memory.

More than 400 people a year in Scotland are diagnosed with the condition, most of them in the western area of the country, which is brought on not by the alcohol but by withdrawal caused when a drinker cuts their alcohol intake suddenly.

Last year the Scottish Executive launched a £1.5m advertising campaign to highlight the dangers of binge drinking after it was revealed that one in 10 of all accident and emergency admissions are attributed to excess drink.

AUBURN, CA -- Attorney Bill McPike confronted the Placer County District Attorney's Office in court on April 29, 2005, to demand a copy of the alleged DEA report that was used to obtain the search warrant to raid the home of former Libertarian candidate for Governor, Steve Kubby in 1999. The DEA report was cited in a search warrant request as evidence that a guest in the Kubby home, Pete Brady, was identified by the DEA as a Jamaican drug smuggler.

The DEA has since confirmed to Mr. Brady in two letters that it had no such report.

Deputy DA Christopher Cattran responded by a last minute filing, at the hearing, of a 35 page brief that gave numerous reasons why the court should not require the DA to produce the DEA report. No DEA report was included in the response filed by Deputy DA Cattran and signed by Placer County District Attorney Bradford Fenocchio.

As shown in court, Pete Brady was actually a journalist, who was interviewing Mr. Kubby for Cannabis Culture magazine. Mr. Brady had never been to Jamaica and is fair skinned with blonde hair. It wasn't until several years after the Kubby case had been heard that Mr. Brady gave Mr. Kubby copies of letters from the DEA denying that any such report ever existed.

" Committing fraud in order to obtain a search warrant to raid a legal medical marijuana patient is a breach of law that threatens everyone, " said Mr. Kubby. " Nobody is safe if the police and prosecutors are free to make up evidence to obtain convictions. Anyone who believes in the rule of law should be alarmed and outraged by the evasive and unethical behavior of the DA in refusing to deal with the real facts of this issue. "

At the hearing, Judge John Cosgrove said that before Mr. McPike can get to the issue of fraud committed upon the court, he must overcome the procedural objections filed by the Placer DA. Mr. McPike said he would not be rushed by the DA's late filing and would need time to study the objections submitted by the DA. However, Mr. McPike made it clear to Judge Cosgrove that the failure of the DA to provide the DEA report remains the key issue, since a conviction obtained through fraud is legally void.

Speaking from his home in British Columbia, Mr. Kubby said he was disturbed by the failure of the DA to provide the DEA report. " The DA is claiming we are in the wrong court and other such nonsense, but we have every right to go back to the court of original jurisdiction with evidence that a fraud was committed by Placer County officials in order to illegally obtain a search warrant.

Certainly, if the report really existed, the DA could have easily found it in their records and produced it for the court to end this matter. However, since the DA has failed to produce the DEA report, we can only assume that he is hiding behind court rules, in order to cover up real and serious violations of the law by himself and others. Until now our suspicions were mostly confined to the arresting officer as the source of the fraud, but these evasive actions by the DA are alarming and suggests a full blown coverup is in progress, " said Mr. Kubby.

Also inserted into Friday's pleadings was the mention of a grand jury complaint being filed by the Kubbys, regarding money still not returned by the police. The Kubbys have documentation that shows the police inventoried $2,300 in cash at the time of the arrest, but have yet to return the money, even though all marijuana charges were dismissed nearly five years ago and a return of property order was issued by the court.

All of the Kubby property, over 200 inventoried items, including legal grow lights has been returned. However the Placer County Sheriff has been unable to locate the Kubby's $2,300. cash. This is missing.

The Kubbys find the missing cash to be very suspicious and want to know who in the Sheriff's Dept. could have inventoried this cash and then misplaced it.

" Perhaps the Placer County Grand Jury in its investigation can locate the missing cash. The issue of missing cash always calls in the question of public honesty and the police purpose for not wanting to end the War on Drugs. one must wonder if this missing cash is part of the reason for the DA's stonewalling on producing the non-existent DEA report on Mr. Brady. It is amazing that the DA would not simply produce this report to clear the air, under the missing cash circumstances. This has fueled the " cover up " theorists who are speculating about the final outcome and who got the Kubby's cash, " said Mr. Kubby

A new hearing date has been set for May 16th at 8:30 am in Department 4 on the 2nd floor of the Historic Courthouse in Auburn, California.
